title: SchemaCatalog
description: The catalog `duckduckgo-search-cli schema` writes when called with no `--name`, discriminated by `type: "schema_catalog"`. The catalog describes every OTHER published contract, and until v1.0.3 it was the one envelope with no contract of its own — the index was the only page missing from the index. Added under GAP-SCHEMA-INTROSPECTION-UNDECLARED-001. English-only: these keys are catalog metadata, not search-result fields.

version.description: Crate version. The catalog is compiled in with `include_str!`, so it matches this binary exactly and cannot drift from it at runtime.

count.description: Number of entries in `schemas`. Redundant with the array length on purpose, so a truncated read is detectable.

id.description: Schema id, which is the file name under `docs/schemas/` without the `.schema.json` suffix.

invoke.description: The exact command that prints this schema body, so an agent can chain discovery to retrieval without constructing argv itself.

discriminator.description: The `type` value carried by envelopes this schema describes. Present only for schemas whose envelope has one: read `type` off an envelope, find the entry declaring it, fetch that schema. Absent means the envelope is identified by the subcommand that produced it — `locale` and `config list` carry no `type` at all — or that the schema describes a file rather than an envelope. Added in v1.0.3 so the routing rule is queryable data instead of knowledge the agent has to hold.

discriminator_key.description: The KEY the discriminator lives under, emitted together with `discriminator` and never alone. Added in v1.0.4: publishing the value without the key was half a routing table. Almost every envelope uses `type`, but `deep-research-output` uses `kind`, so an agent reading `type` on the largest envelope in the product found nothing and had no way to learn why.

routing.description: Why this schema has NO discriminator, present only when `discriminator` is absent. Added in v1.0.4 as free prose; made STRUCTURED in v1.0.5, because the prose mixed three different situations in one string and the facts inside it — which parent `$ref`s a fragment, which keys identify a shape — were unverifiable claims no test could check. As data they are checked: a declared parent must really reference the child, and declared keys must really appear in the schema's `required`.

kind.description: `fragment`: never emitted alone, reached only through `$ref` from `parent`. `shape_routed`: emitted alone and recognised by the required keys in `identified_by`. `not_an_envelope`: describes something other than stdout output, explained in `reason`.

parent.description: Schema id that `$ref`s this fragment. Present only when `kind` is `fragment`.

identified_by.description: Required keys a consumer matches to recognise this envelope without a discriminator. Present only when `kind` is `shape_routed`.

reason.description: What the document describes instead of an envelope. Present only when `kind` is `not_an_envelope`.
